newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed down at 8.3013 against the U.S. dollar in active trading on Thursday due to intervention by the central bank on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market, dealer said.
The yuan opened up at an intra-day high of 8.2987 but soon fell below the 8.3000 level to consolidate around 8.3010 for most of the session, hitting a intraday low of 8.3018.
Trading was more active than on Wednesday, with most done at 8.3010, traders said.
"The People's Bank of China pushed the yuan below 8.3000 after it opened higher on expectations that the yuan will rise by the end of the year," one dealer said.

On Thursday, official newspapers quoted research by the exchange as saying that the yuan would continue its slow rise against the dollar for the rest of the year due to a continued foreign exchange surplus.
"But intervention by the central bank will have more impact on the yuan's movement than China's trade situation," a second dealer said.
Dealers expect the yuan to move below 8.30 on Friday.
The yuan closed down slightly at 7.4386 from 7.4270 against 100 Japanese yen and up at 1.0732 from 1.0737 against the Hong Kong dollar.
